questions.title: "What Does ‘Non‑Uniform Positional Interpolation’ Mean?
questions.question_body:
"Section &#35 discusses ‘non‑uniform’ in two contexts:
•   Dimension non‑uniformity—different ROPE frequencies (θ℃…slow/fast variation).
•   Token‑position non‑uniformity—preserving an initial prefix (τ)—unchanged during down‑scaling.
"The distinction matters because an identical interpolated scale applied uniformly destroys relative distance info differently along high versus low frequency channels;
the preservation of early‐tokens stabilises strong prefixes where attention masses concentrate."

questions.title: "Why impose a monotonic constraint \(\lambda_i \leq \lambda_{i+1}\)?"
questions.question_body:
"The evolutionary optimiser checks whether every sampled vector obeys \(\lambda_0 \leq \lambda_1 \leq … \leq \lambda_{d/2-1}\).
Why is this ordering enforced?
Does it stem simply from speed (reducing infeasible candidates),
or does it reflect neuro‑tangent kernel theory where higher dimensions capture lower spatial frequencies and therefore benefit more aggressive down‑scaling?
Any intuition behind needing monotony instead of arbitrary scale assignments would help me understand its necessity."

questions.title: "How Do λ Rescaling Factors Connect PI, NTK and YaRN Methods?
questions.question_body:
"Equation (4) rewrites ROPE angles generally:
cos(ℓ(n)/βⁱ)… → cos((ℓ/×…)⋯).
With ℓ = n/(λᵢβⁱ).
If π must set ℓ = sn/(βⁱ ), this corresponds to choosing λᵢ = s.
For NTK one picks λᵢ = sⁱ.
YaRN assigns three fixed regimes:
high frequencies λᵢ ≈ 1(normal extrapolation), low frequencies λᵢ≈s
and intermediate ones λᵢ≈sⁱ.
Understanding these exact formula mappings shows why our unified optimisation simply subsumes all previous approaches
and explains how letting every dimension choose its own ℓ uncovers better solutions.”

questions.title: "Why Preserve Initial Tokens Without Scaling During Interpolation?…"
questions.question_body:
"Section &#36 shows experiments keeping ‑𝑛⁠ tokens untouched (λ = 1).
These blocks become anchors almost identical to the pretrained window.
Because most transformers place highest attention scores around the very beginning segments
(a fact reported in Streaming LLAMA
and LM-Infinite papers), keeping their rotational periods intact maintains clearer positional cues.
In contrast, uniformly shrinking all angles crowds later tokens—and corrupts early‑stage representations forever.
The empirical gains shown in Table &#39 display exact evidence.”

questions.title: "Search Space Upper Bound Λmax = s×1\.25 – What’s its Purpose?
questions.question_body:
“In practice λ spans [*exact unit*, *s·1\.25*]. Junction “extra” contraction (> minimum s)
is useful when blindly tightening later positions exerts too much angular compression,
a space where tiny adjustments improve downstream FLOP signals.
Bounding at *s· ¹⋅²⋅⁵* keeps exploration reasonable while admitting modest aggressive compression;
it was chosen empirically – larger ceilings produced almost identical perplexities yet dramatically increased fitness evaluations.”

questions.title: "Progressive Extension From 128 k → 256 k → 2048 k Explained Stepwise︎"
"Recovering Short Context Performance After a Huge Extension Process Ordinance…"
questions.question_body:
“After reaching *L′*=2048 000 attuned models performed poorly under the native *4096*
handle (the infamous crowding problem).
Our remedy performs a *secondary evolution run* constrained specifically at x ∈ {4096,…}.
naturematically it outputs a fresh set {λ(boolean)} tuned so vectors occupy wider angular range when evaluating short sequences.
wheras inference dynamically selects whichever Λ-set matches current max input length (<8192 tiles). Implementation merely substitutes a lookup table stored alongside model configs before ROPE computation.”

questions.title: "Do LongRoPE Modifications Affect Other Parts Of The Transformer Architecture?…"
questions.question_body:
“No invasive changes occur.
applied­ROPE merely replaces factor(s)
untiling every query/key/value pair’s rotary projection:
cross-product ⊙ ⇒ [(sin …,cos …), …]
as usual.
the rest remains identical—including head counts, feed-forward widths, kerning matrices—all fixed weights retain shape licence.“

questions.title: "How Is Perplexity Computed Efficiently During Search Evaluations?…"
questions.question_body:
“During optimisation every candidate collection defines ℓ̃¹,…ℓ̃ⁿ matrices;
a fixed mini‑batch (~5 validation samples)
is passed through whole transformer slowed very few forward passes owing~≤256 per candidate.
a distributed micro CPU cluster parallelizes candidates so multiple lures survive simultaneously.
before lens ≈100% fast enough even when fabricating thousands candidate candidates.”
